text: The Anonymous Was A Woman Award is a grant program for women artists over 40 years of age, established in 1996 to counter sexism in the art world in response to the National Endowment for the Arts' decision to stop funding individual artists. The award provides a grant of $25,000 and is given to exceptional women artists based on their past accomplishments, originality, artistic growth, and the quality of their work. Since its inception, more than 300 women have received the award, with a total of approximately $6.5 million USD distributed. The award was founded by a New York artist who initially remained anonymous and named it after a line from Virginia Woolf's book *A Room of One's Own*, honoring women artists throughout history who have stayed anonymous. Nominators, including art writers, curators, art historians, and previous winners, also remain unnamed. In July 2018, Susan Unterberg was revealed as the founder and funder of the award; prior to that, she had remained anonymous to ensure her artwork was evaluated without bias from her own contributions. In an interview, she stated that it was a good time for women to speak up and that she now feels better equipped to advocate for the cause and encourage both philanthropists and women artists, with plans to expand the program to include seminars. The exhibition *Anonymous Was A Woman: The First 25 Years*, curated by Nancy Princenthal and Vesela Sretenović, will be held at the Grey Art Museum at New York University from April 1 to July 19, 2025, and was published on January 1, 2025, by the Grey Art Museum and Hirmer Verlag. In fall 2025, the Kreeger Museum in Washington, D.C. will host *Anonymous Was a Woman: Jae Ko | linn meyers | Joyce J. Scott | Renée Stout*, featuring works by these four grant recipients, all based in the Washington, D.C. area, curated by Dr. Vesela Sretenović. A list of the award winners is also provided.
